why: Every named file exists in the tracked tree: bin/csv2json.js, src/parse.js, README.md, test/ (csv.test.js) and package.json's `npm test` script (`node --test`). The issue names one function, parse(text, sep = ','), and it matches src/parse.js exactly. The problem's claims are accurate. The CLI calls `parse(readFileSync(0,'utf8'))` and never reads argv, so it "ignores all arguments". I traced `printf 'a\tb\n1,5\tx\n'` by hand: the header becomes ["a\tb"] and the first row ["1","5\tx"], which gives `[{"a\tb":"1"}]` as stated. The no-flag tab case gives `[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]`, which also checks out. The README does show only CSV usage. The --tsv flag and the README and test additions are things the issue asks to create. No named file, command or function is invented.
